"Ravens X2" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $20,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold one of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Everything above about "Ravens X2" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.

810.body:
"In the Green" is down to three top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed yesterday. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

The numbers for "In the Green" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
810.headline: Someone claimed a $50,000 prize

811.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "Extreme Green", about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

The most common prize left on "Extreme Green" right now is $20.

Today's free summary of "Extreme Green" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
811.headline: The prize mix in this game

812.body:
One of Loose Change®'s top prizes was claimed earlier this week. A player in Maryland won $1,000. The game started with 24 top prizes and now has fourteen top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Every line of Loose Change®'s prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
812.headline: A top prize was just claimed

813.body:
"The Price is Right™" has 343,941 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with five left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If you play "The Price is Right™" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
813.headline: A close look at the prizes

814.body:
"High Voltage" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $100,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If "High Voltage" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
814.headline: No top prize claimed lately

815.body:
"$100,000 Crossword" is in the middle of its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

If "$100,000 Crossword" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.

818.headline: A close look at the prizes

819.body:
The prize money on "30X Cash" leans toward the smaller prizes. It is spread over eight prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $30,000. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

The numbers for "30X Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

822.headline: Over a month, no top prize claimed

823.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Holly-Day Cash", about three-quarters are still unsold. The game is about halfway through its run, with seven of seven top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything here about "Holly-Day Cash" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through November 27.
